prompts.task: Use $otel-instrument for a focused, read-only logging repair plan for ./service. Read the real baseline app.js and manifest separately from eval/inputs/logging-contract-evidence.json. The evidence is a synthetic candidate overlay with supplied observations, not live execution or actual baseline instrumentation. Assess every observation and control case against OpenTelemetry logging guidance and the stated operator policy. Identify concrete faults with evidence and the smallest safe language-specific repair and acceptance test; distinguish SDK-owned defaults, unsupported/unverified capability, legitimate opt-ins and optional absent fields from missing application wiring. Save supplemental ./service/.observe/logging-instrument.json and ./service/.observe/logging-instrument.md with per-observation and per-control decisions, reasoning, source citations, and exact future tests. For this explicitly plan-only evaluation do not produce or alter canonical audit/selection/instrumentation reports, edit source/dependencies/config/tests, install packages, execute applications/probes, use network/cloud/models/browser, or claim any runtime/receipt test passed. Do not widen scope to the baseline service general instrumentation gaps. Keep actual runtime verification Not run/Not proven. Use JSON as the detailed supplemental decision/acceptance handoff and Markdown as a concise linked index and summary; do not duplicate the whole plan. There is no fixed word cap. Preserve every applicable concrete obligation, with compact observation/control decisions and shared scenarios by ID. Before finalizing, read back both saved reports against the shared logging reference acceptance table: named bridge/provider owner; exact record/context/real-span checks; named limits plus explicit below/at/above outcomes and units; queue/batch/schedule and final-log receipt/overload checks; observed versus proposed whole deadlines; diagnostic mechanism and configured-signal status; dependency preparation, source/command/version binding, actual pass/fail/error/skip counts, failed timeout/output/cleanup/incremental results. Correct omissions before claiming a complete handoff. Also reconcile the supplied official source_catalog with source/applicability/owner/evidence classifications, assess correlation-join, and distinguish actual real-span joins from injected IDs and legitimate unsampled/outside-span controls. Save the compact source-to-evidence matrix in these supplemental reports. This is still offline and plan-only; cite supplied source provenance without claiming fresh network or runtime verification. Assess the language-options proposal using the detected stack's existing language reference: reject foreign SDK options and unauthorized provider replacement, preserve resource/processors, and give a concrete project-compatible mechanism with unknown installed support still unverified.

judge_inputs: Inspect service/.observe/logging-instrument.json and .md, original source and eval/inputs/logging-contract-evidence.json; inspect trace.jsonl, grade.json and last_message.md. This is explicitly plan-only; never demand an executed runtime or canonical reports. Control cases prevent treating optional or SDK-owned behavior as missing.
rubric: Keeps baseline source facts separate from synthetic overlay observations, writes only supplemental requested reports, covers every observation and control case, cites concrete evidence, and makes no installation/runtime/delivery success claims. Uses the loaded skill and its applicable guidance; current installed capability remains unverified. Writes both supplemental reports under the explicitly requested ./service/.observe directory, not workspace-root .observe. The detailed JSON and concise Markdown index must agree and jointly retain the full applicable acceptance contract; do not reward repetition or a shorter report that omits concrete obligations. A correct linked summary need not repeat every JSON assertion.

Finds the event timestamp overwritten by observed/export time and incorrect numeric ERROR=8; proposes retaining occurrence precision and source severity via the detected official bridge, ERROR in 17-20 range, unknown optional severity not fabricated. For Node explicitly avoids Number precision loss for nanosecond timestamps. Does not require equality of event and observation times.

Identifies missing unsampled log under default trace_based=false and stale IDs after detach; proposes exact in-span sampled/unsampled IDs and flags plus no-context and concurrent/async isolation tests. Preserves explicitly supported operator trace_based=true drops in the explicit-filter control; does not force sampling or fabricate spans to satisfy correlation.

Finds privacy exposure in body, stack and error.dump, replaces invented exception mapping with allowed exception.type where applicable, and omits disallowed message/stack. Applies privacy before export including nested/formatter paths. Does not force EventName or instrumentation-specific exception-event migration/severity onto the existing bridge; ordinary messages and bridge-exception controls are valid without EventName. Removes the observation's unapproved error.kind alias under its strict exception allowlist, but preserves approved-alias control where that separate policy explicitly permits it; unrelated application metadata is not automatically forbidden.

Finds mismatch with selected body/attribute policy; explains span limits do not bound log attributes and log attribute value limits do not bound Body. Plans supported log-specific limits or public API with separate body policy, oversized boundary tests, and accounting where supported. Treats sdk-owned control as covered by defaults/tests rather than demanding application overrides, arbitrary new limits or an additional provider. Names the actual supported count/value configuration fields or public API options instead of only numeric targets; supplies below-limit, exactly-at-limit and above-limit inputs with units and expected outcomes. Unknown installed support remains explicitly unverified; adequate defaults stay covered. Also assesses language-options: rejects the supplied foreign SDK configuration shape for the detected language and its replacement-provider fallback; names the correct native public limit mechanism on the existing owner path, preserving service resource and existing processors. Unknown installed capability requires a concrete source/API-resolution step, not a claimed execution or dependency upgrade. A blanket rejection of all limits, generic numbers without native API names, or replacing the provider fails this criterion.

Finds unbounded log queue, span-only BSP settings, unbounded shutdown, and false complete claim despite two partial-success rejections. Plans bounded log batching/settings via supported BLRP or public APIs, batch<=queue, fault/overload and final-log shutdown tests. Counts 3 attempted, 1 accepted, 2 rejected separately; does not claim durable/exactly-once delivery or infer receipt from enqueue/HTTP200/flush.

Finds recursive exporter diagnostics and halted app progress; proposes separate diagnostic routing or SDK suppression and an outage test proving bounded diagnostics/export attempts, continued application/original sink and unaffected configured signals. Keeps the existing language-specific provider/bridge owner and local-only destination, rather than adding a duplicate SDK/bridge or sending logs to cloud.

Assesses async-handoff as a concrete context-loss observation: capture caller context before scheduling, check exact request-to-record IDs/flags under concurrency, detach/reuse/error/cancel cleanup, and the supplied language-specific boundary. For Java handle approved MDC separately and restore it; for Java/Python inspect bridge placement relative to logging queues. Preserve existing-propagation control without requiring duplicate wrappers/bridges. Expected-loss controls do not make unsafe paths correct.

Rejects the verification-evidence all-pass claim: source revision mismatch invalidates current-source coverage, trial 2 has no fresh execution despite rc=0 and old XML total, trial 3 timed out without a durable structured result. Plans unique report storage, actual pass/fail/error/skip counts, source/command/dependency binding, dependency preparation, timeout output/cleanup and incremental partial results; preserves plan-only Not run and does not call old fixture evidence a current application pass.

For the stalled-receiver delivery observation, distinguishes the 200ms attempt timeout from the 60s retry path with no caller deadline, and proposes a supported whole-operation budget meeting the selected 1000ms policy plus an actual stalled-receiver test. Does not infer all records dropped from client timeout; keeps delivery unknown until an independent receipt resolves it. Preserves bounded-export-default without forcing a redundant application timeout, and recognizes that a timed-out client can coexist with a later accepted record. Shows observed attempt, retry/backoff and absent caller/processor deadline values with units/source separately from the proposed or retained complete budget/mechanism; a new timeout value without this causal before/after distinction is insufficient.

Reconciles the supplied official source catalog in a compact source-to-evidence matrix with requirement level, applicability, SDK/bridge/application/operator owner, coverage state and exact future proof. Rejects correlation-join completeness: ordinary trace_id/span_id attributes do not populate canonical OTLP fields, and matching only TraceId or the wrong parent SpanId cannot prove the active child join. Plans a real SDK-created sampled parent/child span plus application-logger/async test joining exact received IDs, SDK flags, parentage and resource identity; injected contexts alone do not prove startup/export. Preserves unsampled-no-export and outside-request controls without fabricated IDs, forced sampling, duplicate providers or mandatory IDs/EventName on all logs. Separates non-OTLP formatter correlation, SDK/default coverage, application wiring and receipt/backend proof; omitted applicable source rows keep the relevant completeness claim partial. Apply source ownership and applicability: for unknown or optional development SDK capabilities, a concrete future source/API-resolution step and conditional test with unverified status is appropriate; do not demand application overrides or activation of unselected features. Non-OTLP formatter tests are conditional on that selected collection/format path, and must not be substituted for canonical OTLP join proof. Also assesses split-async-join-proof: rejects the combined-coverage claim because known-context async handoff and an independent synchronous real-SDK join do not exercise the same worker/callback log-to-received-span path. Marks that combined claim partial/unproven rather than inventing an application defect from missing evidence. Names one concrete future joint scenario that traverses the owned language boundary with real SDK parent/child context and joins that worker/callback application log canonical TraceId+SpanId, actual SDK flags, parentage and resource at the receiver. The child may begin before dispatch or in the worker according to the real path; preserve provider/bridge ownership and existing propagation, without requiring new production spans or unowned operations solely for proof. Merely referencing separate async and synchronous join scenarios fails this joint obligation. Installed support remains conditional/unverified and plan-only execution remains Not run.
